title: Some and any, adjectives, adverbs and prepositions
matching: Typed answers ignore letter case, extra spaces, apostrophe style and final . ! or ? punctuation. Accents and every other character count. Multiple-choice answers must match exactly.

lessons.title: Some and any with count and non-count nouns
lessons.explanation: Use some in positive statements and any in negative statements and questions. Both work with plural count nouns (apples) and non-count nouns (water, milk, bread): I have some apples. I don't have any milk. Do you have any bread? Non-count nouns have no plural and no a/an: not a milk. Some can also appear in offers, but at this level keep to the basic rule.

pt.title: Some e any com substantivos contáveis e incontáveis
pt.explanation: Use some em frases afirmativas e any em frases negativas e perguntas. Os dois podem ser usados com substantivos contáveis no plural (apples) e incontáveis (water, milk, bread): I have some apples. I don't have any milk. Do you have any bread? Substantivos incontáveis não têm plural e não usam a/an: não diga a milk. Some também pode aparecer em ofertas, mas, neste nível, fique com a regra básica.

lessons.title: Describing with adjectives and comparatives
lessons.explanation: Adjectives describe people and things and stand after be or before a noun: My brother is tall. Make the comparative with -er for short adjectives: tall, taller; old, older; big, bigger (double the final consonant); happy, happier (y becomes i). Use more for longer adjectives: more interesting. Good is irregular: good, better. Use than to compare: This bag is bigger than that bag.

examples.en: This bag is bigger than that bag.

lessons.title: Adverbs of frequency and place
lessons.explanation: Frequency adverbs (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) stand before the main verb and after be: I always drink tea. She is never late. Place adverbs (here, there, outside, inside, upstairs) usually come at the end of the clause: The children play outside. Do not put a frequency adverb between a verb and its object: not I drink always tea.

pt.title: Advérbios de frequência e de lugar
pt.explanation: Advérbios de frequência (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) aparecem antes do verbo principal e depois de be: I always drink tea. She is never late. Advérbios de lugar (here, there, outside, inside, upstairs) normalmente aparecem no fim da oração: The children play outside. Não coloque um advérbio de frequência entre o verbo e seu objeto: não diga I drink always tea.

lessons.title: Prepositions of place and time
lessons.explanation: Use at with clock times (at seven o'clock), on with days (on Monday) and in with months (in June). For place, on means touching the top of a surface (on the table), in means inside (in the box), under means below, next to means beside and between means in the middle of two things. Learn these as chunks: at home, on Monday, in June.

examples.en: The book is on the table.
The class starts at seven o'clock.

pt.title: Preposições de lugar e de tempo
pt.explanation: Use at com horários exatos (at seven o'clock), on com dias (on Monday) e in com meses (in June). Para lugar, on indica contato com a superfície (on the table), in indica que algo está dentro (in the box), under significa abaixo, next to significa ao lado e between indica que algo está no meio de duas coisas. Aprenda essas combinações como blocos: at home, on Monday, in June.
